findings.reason: Verified in topic_user.rb: TopicUser.change sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, while the new action only saves notification_level, so auto_track (which only fires when the reason is nil) can later bump the muted topic back to tracking.
Verified that TopicUser.find_by returns nil for a user with no row and tu.notification_level is then called without a nil guard, so a logged-in user with access but no row gets a 500.
Verified the state-changing GET route with no CSRF protection, and each request steps the level down again (watching to regular to muted), so a cross-site image or a reload can change the level.
Verified in application_controller.rb that a non-JSON GET raised NotLoggedIn redirects to '/' without unsubscribing or returning to the URL, so the email link silently fails for logged-out users.

Verified loadTopicView fetches the plain /t/:id.json when PreloadStore misses, so an in-app entry shows the 'stop receiving' text without changing anything, but the in-app entry path is unconfirmed and the finding itself is hedged.
Verified the controller sets regular (not muted) when the level is above regular, while the locale string always says notifications stop, so the wording is misleading in that case.

The spec only adds unsubscribe_url to avoid an interpolation failure, and no controller spec covers the new action, which is a real test gap on a non-critical path with no named defect it would catch.
The misspelling 'stopNotificiationsText' is confirmed in the controller and template, but it is a naming issue only.
